rules: A spinner shows that something is loading or working when its duration is unknown and its place is small (inside a control, next to a label, in an empty panel). A known amount of progress is a Progress; a placeholder of the content to come is a Skeleton.

The container is a square of size; track is a full ring and indicator a quarter arc of the same ring, both drawn with a stroke of 1/9 of size (2.5 units in a 24-unit box with a ring of radius 9, the drawing of the Button loading indicator) and rounded ends.

Both parts are drawn in the current content color, inherited from the surrounding content: indicator at full opacity, track at trackOpacity. The spinner therefore reads on any surface its parent's content color is designed for.
The indicator turns clockwise around the center at one turn per motionDuration, linearly and without end. When reduced motion is requested it turns three times slower.
Sizes follow the icon scale (sm 16, md 20, lg 24, xl 32 px in the reference set) and do not change with density.

With an empty label the spinner is decorative and hidden from assistive technology: the element that is loading states it (a busy Button, a busy region). With a non-empty label the spinner is exposed as a status whose accessible name is label, announced politely once when it appears.
The spinner is not interactive: it is never focusable and emits no events.
In forced-colors mode both parts are drawn in the system text color, the track keeping trackOpacity.
